items.statement: For every finite-dimensional complete real Hilbert/Borel space E, including rank zero, let gamma be literal stdGaussian E. Every signed real globally C2 f with actual f in L2(gamma), true gradient f in L2(gamma), and Phi(f²) integrable satisfies homogeneous Ent_gamma(f²)<=2 integral norm(gradient f)^2. The actual cutoff mass, entropy and gradient-energy limits are proved internally. Phi(t)=t log t is continuous at zero; neither positive mass nor normalization nor compact support is assumed.
assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional complete real Hilbert space with compatible Borel measurable structure; rank0 is permitted.
f is signed globally C2; actual MemLp f2 and MemLp true gradient f2 hold under literal gamma.
Actual Phi(f²) is Integrable gamma. These domain predicates are real32 outputs at the paper consumer, not extra FIRST premises or limit certificates.
Real Bochner integrals use true L1 domains; coefficient2 is variance1 Gaussian, with homogeneous entropy allowing mass0.

steps.title: Derive genuine square and energy domains
steps.text: The two genuine L2 hypotheses imply square and Hilbert-gradient-energy L1. The entropy L1 is the third analytic-domain premise. C2 gives continuity and the true Riesz-gradient measurability needed below; no totalized-integral fallback is used.
steps.formula: f\in L^2(\gamma),\ \nabla f\in L^2(\gamma),\ \Phi(f^2)\in L^1(\gamma)\ \Longrightarrow\ f^2,\|\nabla f\|^2\in L^1(\gamma).

steps.title: Construct actual compact approximants
steps.text: Use the canonical radial cutoff at R_n=n+1, multiply by f, and derive C2compact regularity. One positive derivative constant C is chosen before all radii. Range[0,1] and the real neighborhood plateau come from the same actual cutoff.

steps.title: Bound the true gradient and identify its limit
steps.text: Apply the real product derivative and Riesz inverse, whose isometry identifies derivative norm with gradient norm. With R_n>=1, the square energy is dominated by2G²+2C²f². For each point the cutoff equals1 on a neighborhood for all sufficiently large radii, so its product has exactly the original true gradient there, including rank0.
steps.formula:
abla f_n=\chi_n

abla\chi_n,\quad\|
abla f_n\|^2\le2\|
abla f\|^2+2C^2f^2,\quad

steps.title: Control entropy even where the density vanishes
steps.text: The totalized zero-aware product identity gives Phi(aq)=aPhi(q)+qPhi(a). For0<=a<=1, the lower bound a-1<=Phi(a) and Phi(a)<=0 imply |Phi(a)|<=1. With a=chi_n² and q=f² this gives an integrable dominator without taking log of f or dividing by mass.

steps.title: Prove all three real integral limits
steps.text: Apply dominated convergence separately with q, |Phi(q)|+q and2G²+2C²q. Every sequence is strongly measurable through actual continuity, every dominator is L1 from the analytic domains, and the pointwise limits are proved using the actual cutoff and gradient plateau.

steps.title: Pass the compact inequalities without changing the constant
steps.text: Apply actual compact41LSI to each f_n. Continuity of Phi at the limiting mass, including mass0, gives the homogeneous entropy limit. Closed-order convergence passes the inequalities with the unchanged coefficient2.

steps.title: Exercise the actual noncompact posterior
steps.text: The true standardizedRGO theorem supplies C2, fL2, gradientL2 and qlogqL1 at its actual proximal witness, with f²=q. The Test applies this new result to the raw f=exp(-rho/2)/sqrtZ, without a cutoff certificate or upper step-size restriction. The distinct33KL witness must still be reconciled; GaussianT2/FIRST4.6 remain separate.
